items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: I used to like to listen to John Coltrane or Miles Davis play

ctx.x: No I don’t think so. I don’t think so. Basically the jazz funerals were sort of designated from musicians so it didn’t make any sense. Because you have a service going on in the church and then outside there’s another thing going on. So whatever goes on in the church, that’s that service or whatever. Outside it has no denomination whatsoever. And so usually outside there are people talking and the brass band around waiting, and you know just waiting for the service inside the church to come out. So sometimes I…

my grandson, and I played a gig the following weekend in the East Village at this St. Mark’s Center. And the feeling and the love that was in that center at St. Mark’s was I felt like I was in the church in New Orleans because it was more a thing of poets and writers who came together to pay homage to New Orleans and Katrina and their words just portrayed how they felt about it. Some were angry about it. Some were beautiful, just peaceful. I performed after Toni Morrison, the great writer. And man she is one of…
Did it affect the way you performed that day do you think?
